results.reasoning: Judged headless from the working-tree CLI (node bin/walkdown.js) against throwaway git repositories under a scratchpad, each with its own private HOME and WALKDOWN_HOME, so neither the real personal config nor this repository was ever in scope. The rule's own scenario holds cleanly and that belongs on the record first: with the person's words above and below the block and the spec then moved (`init --commit none` out of the repository, `init --commit spec` back in, which is the only way the spec moves - `walkdown move` takes runs/threads/evidence/drafts and refuses `spec`), placing the pointer again rewrote the block in place, and the unified diff of the whole file is one changed line naming the new place with every other byte identical; the block appeared exactly once; and a second placement reported `already current` and left the file md5-identical. A duplicated block was not reachable through walkdown's own commands either - `init` refuses to guess when several agent files exist, and following its own advice into a symlinked AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md pair found the block it had just written and reported up-to-date rather than appending a second. What fails is narrower, and it is the literal promise 'nothing else in that file'. placePointer resumes the person's text at `text.slice(to + POINTER_END.length + 1)` (lib/init.js:150, and the same expression in the equality test at :148), which assumes exactly one newline follows its own end marker and swallows whatever character is actually there. Three files where it is not a newline, all in the boundary-probes evidence: trailing whitespace on the end-marker line leaves behind a new line holding a single space; a CRLF file - an ordinary Windows checkout, or core.autocrlf - loses the CR and gains a blank line the person never wrote between the block and their next line; and a person's own HTML comment written after the marker loses its leading angle bracket and becomes broken markup. None of these accumulate - each stabilises after one run - and none of them mislead an agent about where the spec is, so this is a boundary bug in an otherwise sound design rather than a wrong design. I am calling it fail rather than pass because the statement is absolute about ownership and the third case destroys a character of the person's own text, and because the fix is small: consume to the end of the marker's own line (the next newline after it, or end of file) instead of assuming its length. Filed as n-0187. Recorded in that thread but deliberately not the ground of this verdict: when a file already contains two marker pairs, only the first is rewritten and the second keeps naming the place the spec has left - the exact harm the statement describes - but no walkdown command was found that produces that state, so it needs a person to have pasted the markers themselves.
